correctness.rationale: Vandermonde gives period 3^(k+1); in the r=2 branch g_2(t)≡t coefficientwise modulo 3, so it is an onto isometry and shift 3^k in n fails by exact valuation k−1. For r=0,1, h_r=g_r/3 reduces coefficientwise to ±t(t−1); the derivative has just the simple root t≡2. Expanding at its lift gives h_r(α_r+u)−h_r(α_r)=u²B_r(u) with B_r congruent to the respective sign. The principal square root of the unit after division by that sign has difference divisible by 3(u−v) at two arguments; multiplying it by u gives an onto isometry. Thus each quadratic branch contributes a square-root count modulo 3^(k−1), with three lifts per root in the full period. Evaluating at t=2 gives centers 6 and 3 modulo 9. The two full quadratic-branch images do overlap at 0 mod 9, giving 12 extra indices there. Only the critical subimages are disjoint modulo 9: their supports are β_0+27 Z_3² and β_1−27 Z_3², so removing these and all multiples of 9 gives the exact singleton count. The square density 3/8 gives 31/36. For m=k−1≥3, the unique largest root count is at zero for even m or at 3^(m−1) for odd m, and exceeds the overlap's count of four square roots. Each critical branch produces one maximizer. The formula also gives the three stated initial maxima. Independent modular Pascal recurrence and coefficient-derived Hensel centers agreed at every target for k=1–8, including the maxima and their multiplicities.
residual_risks: In RESULT.md line 79, disjointness modulo nine is valid for the critical subimages, not the full images; the proof in lines 81–89 accounts for the shared ball. The finite comparisons are not the all-depth proof.
